location.mountain: Hills around Sun Moon Lake (Riyue Tan)

characteristics.cultivar: Ruby #18 (hybrid of native wild Taiwanese tea and Burmese var. assamica)

description.short: Unique Taiwanese black tea with natural cooling aromas of cinnamon and fresh mint, specifically bred for the island's terroir
description.overview: The only cultivar in the world bred specifically for black tea by Taiwanese agronomists by crossing an indigenous wild mountain tea tree with a Burmese large-leaf variety — the culmination of decades of dedicated research.
description.leaf: Large, dark, gracefully twisted whole leaves
description.aroma: Distinct natural cinnamon and wintergreen mint notes with a wild honey sweetness — completely unique to this cultivar
description.taste: Naturally sweet, subtly spicy, with pronounced cinnamon-menthol nuances without any added flavorings
description.processing: Plucking → withering → rolling → full oxidation → drying

history.origin: Bred by Taiwan's Tea Research and Extension Station (TRES) by crossing native wild mountain Camellia formosensis with Burmese Assamica; the hybridization program spanned several decades.
history.development: Officially registered as cultivar #18 in 1999 and trade-named 'Ruby' (Hong Yu, 'red jade') for its magnificent radiant liquor.
history.modern: Primarily grown around scenic Sun Moon Lake, it is regarded as a crown jewel of modern Taiwanese agronomic breeding, celebrated for its naturally occurring spices.
interestingFacts: Ruby #18 is one of the few cultivars globally bred purely and specifically for the black tea category rather than multipurpose processing.
Its distinct cinnamon and menthol notes are 100% natural, arising purely from the plant's unique genetic lineage rather than flavored oils or additives.
